newsitem.title: UK: UK's Beckett says won't tighten takeover laws.
newsitem.headline: UK's Beckett says won't tighten takeover laws.

text.p: Britain's Trade and Industry Secretary, Margaret Beckett, said on Tuesday she would shake up competition law but would not introduce legislation to force companies attempting takeovers to justify their actions.
Asked on BBC radio if a law would be passed to force companies to prove a takeover was in the public interest, Beckett replied simply, "No."
"We are going to change competition law to...make competition policy more effective, to make business more competitive and to act more in the interest of the customer," she said.
"But we are not going to make the precise change to which you refer."
Beckett said her department would continue to consult with business, as Labour had done in opposition.

She said it was too early to gauge the latest uncertainties over a single European currency -- a new left-wing French government and the German government's backdown on plans to revalue gold reserves.
"I think it's genuinely too early to say (whether EMU will go ahead in 1999) but obviously these are new developments and we are all waiting to assess what in practice they will mean," she said.
But whatever happened, Beckett said, it was her job to express the business community's opinions about what European economic and monetary union would mean for Britain's economy.
Beckett will give a news conference later on Wednesday, following a speech to industrialists in which she will give her views on competitiveness.
